pharm: Human anti-PD-L1 IgG1 antibody blocking PD-L1/PD-1 interaction with retained ADCC effector function; includes premedication for infusion reactions
quick: 800 mg IV every 2 weeks (maintenance urothelial, MCC); RCC with axitinib per labeling
Can cause fetal harm (immune mechanism); verify status; effective contraception during and for months after last dose
No human milk data; do not breastfeed during treatment and after last dose per labeling
No dose adjustment in mild-moderate impairment; monitor creatinine (immune nephritis)
No adjustment in mild impairment; monitor LFTs (immune hepatitis); limited severe data
No specific interaction; avoid excess with hepatitis risk
Thyroid, LFTs, creatinine, glucose; immune-toxicity review
summary: Avelumab (Bavencio) is an anti-PD-L1 antibody used as switch-maintenance after platinum chemotherapy in advanced urothelial carcinoma (JAVELIN Bladder 100 - survival benefit without progression), for metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma, and with axitinib in advanced renal cell carcinoma. Infusion-related reactions are more frequent than with PD-1 agents, so antihistamine-paracetamol premedication is standard. Immune-mediated toxicities follow the class pattern.
indications: Maintenance treatment of locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma that has not progressed on first-line platinum chemotherapy
Advanced renal cell carcinoma in combination with axitinib (first line)

dosage.d: 800 mg every 2 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.t: IV over 60 minutes with antihistamine + paracetamol premedication for the first 4 infusions (then as needed)
dosage.n: Start within weeks of finishing platinum (maintenance timing matters)

dosage.d: 800 mg every 2 weeks with axitinib 5 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Monitor LFTs closely (axitinib hepatotoxicity overlap); hold/reduce axitinib per its rules

admin: IV infusion over 30-60 minutes per labeling (not IV push); observe for infusion reactions
Baseline labs: CBC, LFTs, creatinine, TFTs, glucose, cortisol/ACTH where indicated; HBV/HCV/TB screen per risk
Grade 2+ immune events: hold drug and start corticosteroids per grade; grade 3-4 usually discontinues (endocrinopathies excepted with hormone replacement)
Do not use immunosuppressive corticosteroids pre-emptively except for chemo-combination antiemesis per protocol
moa: Checkpoint blockade restores anti-tumour T-cell activity as described below; responses can be delayed and pseudoprogression occurs - confirm progression before stopping.

relative: Active autoimmune disease requiring immunosuppression (risk-benefit individualised)
Prior severe immune-mediated toxicity to the same class (rechallenge individualised)

preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: No formal adjustment in mild-moderate impairment; monitor creatinine closely (immune nephritis can mimic AKI).
hepatic: No formal adjustment in mild impairment; monitor LFTs closely (immune hepatitis). Limited data in moderate-severe.

major: Systemic corticosteroids/immunosuppressants (may blunt efficacy if given before response; used to treat toxicity)
moderate: Other hepatotoxic or nephrotoxic agents (overlapping injury patterns)
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; counsel on concomitant risks.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

emergency: Severe immune-mediated reaction with organ failure - hold drug and seek emergency care
Severe infusion reaction with breathing difficulty - seek emergency care

monitoring: Thyroid function at baseline and periodically
Liver enzymes, creatinine and glucose before each dose
Corticosteroid readiness for grade 2+ immune events
Maintenance-timing review (start after platinum response, not at progression)
RCC: LFTs and blood pressure (axitinib overlap)
counsel: Diarrhoea, especially bloody or with cramps, needs same-day reporting (bowel inflammation)
New cough, breathlessness or chest pain needs urgent evaluation (lung/heart inflammation)
Yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine or severe nausea needs urgent liver review
Unusual thirst, frequent urination, severe headache, vision change or profound fatigue can mean hormone-gland inflammation - report promptly
Do not start steroids or stop the cancer drug on your own for side effects - call the team first
Premedication before the drip reduces shivering/fever reactions - attend the full infusion time
Maintenance therapy starts while the cancer is controlled after chemo, not after it regrows
pk: Immune activation within weeks; radiographic response often at 8-12 weeks; pseudoprogression possible
Receptor occupancy persists weeks after dosing; treatment until progression or unacceptable toxicity (adjuvant courses are fixed-duration)
Refrigerate 2-8 C; do not freeze or shake; use diluted infusion promptly per labeling
pearls: Immune toxicities can appear months after starting and even after stopping - the review window stays open
Endocrinopathies (thyroid, type 1 diabetes, hypophysitis) are usually managed with hormone replacement while continuing therapy
Steroids treat the toxicity, not the cancer: grade-based hold/steroid rules are the safety core
Only checkpoint with a proven switch-maintenance survival benefit in urothelial cancer - timing (post-platinum, pre-progression) is the point
Premedicate routinely: infusion reactions exceed PD-1-agent rates; ADCC-competent IgG1 design is the reason cited
missed: If a planned dose is missed, give it as soon as possible and adjust the schedule to maintain the planned interval; do not double the dose. Consult the full prescribing information for cycle-delay rules.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose is expected to exaggerate known toxicities (myelosuppression, GI effects, infusion reactions). Provide supportive care with close monitoring. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
